question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI participants, with structural MRI as the shared channel. P-273's DISFC model is multimodal: 3D sMRI, 14 demographic/cognitive features (MMSE, CDRSB, ADAS11/13, RAVLT, FAQ, mPACC and others) and 49 SNPs, with a 48-month horizon. P-65's HemiNet uses a single-time-point structural MRI only, with a 36-month horizon. Same task, population class and shared channel. The added predictors, the horizon, architecture, sample size and CV design differ; the rule allows these and they are listed as candidate explanations.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (and accuracy with accuracy), both from internal cross-validation on ADNI.

figures.P-273: Trimodal DISFC, 10-fold CV: AUC 0.962 (fold SD 0.041); accuracy 92.92% (SD 4.41%). The CV set is 238 MCI: of the 252 MCI, 94 progressed and 158 stayed stable, and the 14-subject ADNI-3 test set holds 3 pMCI, so the CV set is 91 pMCI / 147 sMCI. Hanley-McNeil for 0.962: Q1 = 0.962/1.038 = 0.9268; Q2 = 2*0.962^2/1.962 = 0.9434; SE^2 = [0.0366 + 90*(0.9268-0.9254) + 146*(0.9434-0.9254)]/(91*147) = 2.775/13377 = 0.000207; SE = 0.0144; interval [0.934, 0.990]. Accuracy, Wilson on n = 238: [0.889, 0.955]. MRI-only unimodal arm, read from Fig. 4B because no number is printed: AUC about 0.802 and accuracy about 0.758. The reading was calibrated against the printed trimodal values, which the bars reproduce (0.963 vs 0.962; 0.927 vs 0.9292), so it is good to about +-0.004. Hanley-McNeil for 0.802 with 91/147: SE = 0.0310; interval [0.741, 0.863] (0.795 gives [0.733, 0.857]; 0.806 gives [0.746, 0.866]). MRI-only accuracy 0.758, Wilson n = 238: [0.700, 0.808].
figures.P-65: HemiNet, 5-fold stratified CV repeated 5 times on 573 subjects (300 pMCI / 273 sMCI): AUC 0.8401 +- 0.0297 (SD across runs; no interval printed); accuracy 0.7819. Hanley-McNeil for 0.8401 with 300/273: Q1 = 0.7243; Q2 = 0.7671; SE^2 = [0.1343 + 299*0.0185 + 272*0.0613]/81900 = 22.35/81900 = 0.000273; SE = 0.0165; interval [0.808, 0.872]. With the run SD used as the spread: [0.782, 0.898]. Accuracy, Wilson n = 573: [0.746, 0.814].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists. P-273's Fig. 4B reports a unimodal MRI model cross-validated 'with identical settings', which is P-65's input condition (MRI only). The recorded gap does not survive on it. P-273's MRI-only AUC (about 0.80) is lower than P-65's 0.840, so the direction reverses. The matched accuracies agree both ways: 0.758 vs 0.782, each inside the other's Wilson interval, two-sample z = 0.73. On AUC, P-65's 0.840 lies inside P-273's MRI-only interval [0.741, 0.863], but 0.802 lies about 0.006 below P-65's Hanley-McNeil lower bound of 0.808 (0.002 to 0.013 across the reading range). It lies inside the interval built from P-65's run SD [0.782, 0.898]. Two-sample z = (0.8401-0.802)/sqrt(0.0310^2+0.0165^2) = 1.09. P-273 also shows where its advantage comes from. Fig. 4B puts MRI-only at about 0.80, MRI+clinical at about 0.94 (the text states the trimodal model beat the MRI+clinical model by 0.022), and trimodal at 0.962. So the added cognitive/clinical inputs account for the whole recorded gap.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion. P-273's 0.962 is below 0.97, and it also reports an ADNI-3 independent test (n = 14, AUC 0.939, 95% CI 0.796-1.000), too small to be informative. P-65's 0.840 comes from 573 subjects with an external OASIS-3 cohort (0.8137). Checked against P-273 pages 6-7 and P-65 Table 3.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-273's figure uses cognitive/clinical scores and SNPs as well as MRI, while P-65 uses MRI alone. P-273's own ablation (Fig. 4B) shows this accounts for the recorded gap, so for the recorded figures the explanation is shown, not merely candidate.
candidate_explanations.quote: The trimodal DISFC model was superior to the top-performing bimodal model using MRI and clinical data with a significant increase of 0.022 (P = 0.048) in AUC

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: conversion within 48 months against within 36 months.
candidate_explanations.quote: The cross-validation set consisted of 238 MCI subjects from ADNI-1 and ADNI-GO/2 cohorts, with a 48-month follow-up.
participants in the pMCI group were initially diagnosed with MCI at baseline and converted to AD within 36 months of follow-up

candidate_explanations.difference: Training data: P-273 adds 45 AD subjects to training.
candidate_explanations.quote: Additionally, 45 subjects with AD were included in the model training to provide insights into pathological changes and address class imbalance.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size, cohort selection and CV design: 238 subjects in 10-fold CV against 573 right-handed subjects in repeated 5-fold CV. Architecture: separable-convolution fusion network against a 3D DenseNet with hemispheric-asymmetry attention.
candidate_explanations.quote: Across the ADNI-1/2/3/GO phases, 573 subjects (300 pMCI and 273 sMCI) were included

reason: The recorded gap (0.962 vs 0.840) exceeds uncertainty both ways (z = 5.6). But P-273 reports its own MRI-only arm, the matched condition, at about 0.80. That value is on the other side of P-65's figure, agrees with it on accuracy (z = 0.73), and on AUC contains P-65's value within its interval. Only the P-65 Hanley-McNeil interval excludes the matched value, by about 0.006, on a number read from a bar chart (z = 1.09). So the papers' own data dissolve the recorded discrepancy, and P-273 shows that its cognitive and genetic inputs account for it. What remains is a small reversed AUC crossing that meets the one-way test only at the edge. This pair is treated like C-76: borderline, not yes. If one-way crossings of this size are read as agreement, the pair is a plain no.

quotes.quote: On the cross-validation set, our model achieved superior results for predicting MCI conversion within 4 years (AUC, 0.962; accuracy, 92.92%; sensitivity, 88.89%; specificity, 95.33%)
a multimodal deep learning model based on 3D sMRI scans, demographic and neuropsychological assessments, and genetic polymorphism data to predict the risk of MCI progression to AD at baseline.
Of the 252 MCI patients, 94 (37.3%) progressed to AD, and 158 (62.7%) remained stable during follow-up.
